questions.stem: A patient was using one of the anti-glaucoma drugs and observed Black deposits on the conjunctiva. The suspected drug known to cause this adverse effect is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Adrenergic agonists

Alpha-2-adrenergic agonists like apraclonidine and brimonidine are used in the treatment of glaucoma.

  • Adrenergic agonists like adrenaline form adrenochrome in the conjunctiva and are responsible for Black deposits in the conjunctiva
  • It penetrates the cornea and is hydrolyzed by the esterases present there into Adrenaline, which itself has poor corneal penetration and causes ocular smarting and reactive hyperemia.
  • They reduce aqueous humor production


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 168

Lid retraction
  • Apraclonidine causes itching, lid dermatitis, follicular conjunctivitis, mydriasis, eyelid retraction, dryness of mouth and nose
  • It decreases aqueous production by primary α2 and subsidiary α1 action in the ciliary body
  • Its use is restricted to short-term control of spikes of i.o.t. after laser trabeculoplasty or iridotomy


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 168

questions.stem: Which of the following is false about Brimonidine?
questions.solutionHtml:
Does not cross BBB
  • Brimonidine is α2 selective and more lipophilic than Apraclonidine, So it Crosses BBB and causes CNS depression
  • Action: Reduces aqueous production
  • Brimonidine is indicated both for short-term (prophylaxis of i.o.t. spikes post laser/post-surgery) as well as long-term use in glaucoma. It is generally used for add-on therapy only.
  • Brimonidine is contraindicated in children <2yrs. It causes brain suppression which leads to apnea.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 168

questions.stem: Which of the following acts by decreasing aqueous humor?
questions.solutionHtml:
Betaxolol
  • Betaxolol acts on beta receptors and decreases aqueous humor formation
  • It has the advantage of less bronchopulmonary and probably fewer cardiac, central, and metabolic side effects.
  • Betaxolol is a beta 1 or cardioselective or 2nd generation beta blocker.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 168

questions.stem: Iris pigmentation is noted with the use of one of the following drugs used in glaucoma:
questions.solutionHtml:
Prostaglandin analogs
  • Prostaglandin analogs cause iris pigmentation, growth of eyelashes, and macular edema
  • Because of good efficacy, once-daily application, and absence of systemic complications, PG analogs have become the first-choice drugs for open-angle glaucoma
  • They act by increasing uveoscleral outflow


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 169

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs can be used in the treatment of hypotrichosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bimatoprost

Prostaglandin analogs have side effects of heterochromia iridis, hypertrichosis, and macular edema. The side effect of hypertrichosis is clinically utilized in patients having hypotrichosis.

  • Prostaglandin analogs cause the growth of eyelashes so can be used in hypotrichosis.
  • Bimatoprost is a synthetic prostamide derivative found to be equally or more effective than latanoprost in lowering i.o.t.
  • No systemic side effects are reported.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 169

questions.stem: A Male with insulin-dependent diabetes having macular edema develops glaucoma. Which drug should be used as the last resort to treat?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prostaglandin analog
  • As the patient already has macular edema, so prostaglandin analogs like latanoprost and bimatoprost can’t be used.
  • Prostaglandin analogs cause Iris pigmentation, growth of eyelashes, and macular edema
  • Macular edema can develop during treatment with any PGF2α analog, especially in aphakic patients
  • A watch should be kept to detect it early.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 169
